heard: Giant clouds of glowing gas dwarf our entire galaxy. Astronomers in 2000 discovered hydrogen blobs spanning 400,000 light years across. Using the Subaru telescope, team members found 30 more along a cosmic filament. Nothing that huge should shine so brightly billions of light years away. Scientists debated if gas was falling in or supernovas were blowing out, but polarized light proved the primary power was hidden inside. Supermassive black holes inside act like cosmic light bulbs, illuminating the gas. These hidden engines explain how giant gas clouds dwarf our galaxy.
